course.title: Boxing Basics
course.tagline: Learn stance, punches and footwork, and train like a boxer from day one.

days.title: What is boxing?
days.goal: Learn what boxing is and what you need to start.

video.title: Basics of Boxing - Training for Beginners at Home

steps: Watch the video and write the main idea in one sentence.
Boxing is a sport of punches, footwork and defence.
You need: space, comfy shoes, hand wraps or gloves if you have them.
Set one goal: learn the stance and the jab this week.
days.task: Write what boxing is in your own words.
days.challenge: List what you need to start boxing at home.

options: A sport of punches, footwork and defence
quiz.explain: Boxing mixes punches, footwork and defence.

quiz.q: What do you need to start?
quiz.explain: Space and shoes are enough to start.

quiz.q: What should your first goal be?
options: Punch as hard as you can
Learn the stance and the jab
quiz.explain: Stance and jab are the safe first steps.

days.title: The boxing stance
days.goal: Learn the stance: how boxers stand.

video.title: How to Box 101 | Complete Boxing Tutorial for Beginners

steps: Stand sideways: one foot forward, one foot back.
Keep your knees soft and your weight balanced.
Raise your hands to guard your face.
Keep your chin down a little.
days.task: Hold the stance for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Practise stepping forward and back in stance.

options: Sideways, one foot forward, one back
quiz.explain: A sideways stance protects the body.
Hands up guard the face.

options: It protects your chin from punches
quiz.explain: A tucked chin is safer.

days.title: The jab: your first punch
days.goal: Learn the jab, the most important punch.

video.title: Beginner to Boxer in 25 Minutes

steps: From your stance, punch straight out with your front hand.
Turn your fist as it goes out.
Snap it back fast to guard.
Keep your other hand up guarding your face.
days.task: Do 20 slow jabs, then 20 faster ones.
days.challenge: Practise the jab in front of a mirror.

options: A quick straight punch with the front hand
quiz.explain: The jab is a fast, straight punch.

quiz.q: What should your other hand do?
quiz.explain: The other hand guards while you jab.

quiz.q: How should a jab come back?
quiz.explain: A fast return keeps you safe.

days.title: The cross: your power punch
days.goal: Learn the cross, a strong straight punch.

video.title: Learn to Box at Home: 5 Days to Master the Basics

steps: From your stance, punch with your back hand.
Turn your back foot and hip as you punch.
Keep your front hand up guarding.
Snap the punch back fast to guard.
days.task: Do 20 slow crosses, then 20 faster ones.
days.challenge: Do jab-cross 10 times: 1-2, 1-2.

options: A straight punch with the back hand
quiz.explain: The cross is a strong straight punch.

quiz.q: What turns when you throw a cross?
quiz.explain: Hip turn gives the cross its power.

options: A jab followed by a cross
quiz.explain: One-two is jab then cross.

days.title: Footwork: move like a boxer
days.goal: Learn to move forward, back and side to side.

video.title: Boxing for Beginners

steps: Step forward with the front foot first, then the back foot.
Step back with the back foot first, then the front foot.
Keep your stance wide and your knees soft.
Never cross your feet.
days.task: Move forward and back 10 times in stance.
days.challenge: Move side to side 10 times in stance.

options: Crossed feet make you lose balance
It is a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: Crossed feet leave you off balance.

quiz.q: Which foot moves first going forward?
quiz.explain: Front foot first keeps the stance wide.
Soft knees keep you balanced and ready.

days.title: The hook: a side punch
days.goal: Learn the hook, a punch that comes from the side.

video.title: Shadow Boxing for Beginners

steps: From your stance, bend your front arm at 90 degrees.
Turn your front foot and hip as you swing.
Keep your elbow up at shoulder height.
Snap the punch back to guard.
days.task: Do 10 slow hooks, then 10 faster ones.
days.challenge: Do jab-cross-hook 5 times.

options: A punch that comes from the side
quiz.explain: A hook swings around from the side.

quiz.q: How bent should your arm be?
quiz.explain: A 90-degree bend makes a strong hook.
Elbow up keeps the hook strong.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your first combo
days.goal: Put week 1 together: build your first punch combo.

video.title: Punching and Footwork for Beginners

steps: Your combo is: jab, cross, hook. That is 1-2-3.
Practise slowly 10 times.
Add footwork: step in, punch, step out.
Do the combo 10 times to a steady beat.
days.task: Do your 1-2-3 combo 10 times.
days.challenge: Do the combo while moving forward and back.

quiz.explain: A combo links punches together.
One-two-three is jab, cross, hook.

quiz.q: Why add footwork to a combo?
options: So you can hit and move safely
quiz.explain: Footwork lets you attack and stay safe.

project.title: Your first combo
project.brief: Build your first punch combo: jab, cross, hook (1-2-3), with footwork, and do it 10 times to a steady beat.

days.title: Defence: block and slip
days.goal: Learn two ways to avoid a punch.

video.title: Learning to Box: The Basics

steps: Block: raise your gloves to catch a punch.
Slip: move your head a little to one side.
Practise slipping left and right slowly.
Always return to guard after a slip.
days.task: Practise 10 slips to the left and 10 to the right.
days.challenge: Block an imaginary punch 10 times.

options: Raising your gloves to catch a punch
quiz.explain: A block stops a punch with your gloves.

options: Moving your head a little to dodge a punch
quiz.explain: A slip dodges a punch with head movement.

quiz.q: What should you do after a slip?
quiz.explain: Returning to guard keeps you safe.

days.title: Shadow boxing: box the air
days.goal: Learn shadow boxing: practise punches without a bag.

video.title: BOXING BASICS (Beginner Friendly)

steps: Stand in front of a mirror in your stance.
Throw jab, cross, hook slowly, watching your form.
Add footwork: move as you punch.
Do 3 rounds of 2 minutes with 1 minute rest.
days.task: Shadow box for 2 minutes in front of a mirror.
days.challenge: Do 3 rounds of shadow boxing.

quiz.explain: Shadow boxing trains form without a bag.

options: So you can see your form
quiz.explain: A mirror shows mistakes in form.

quiz.q: How long should a round be?
quiz.explain: Two-minute rounds suit a beginner.

days.title: The uppercut: punch from below
days.goal: Learn the uppercut, a punch that comes up from below.

video.title: Low Impact Boxing Workout For Beginners

steps: From your stance, drop your back hand a little.
Punch up in a short curve, turning your hip.
Keep your other hand up guarding.
Snap the punch back to guard.
days.task: Do 10 slow uppercuts, then 10 faster ones.
days.challenge: Do jab-cross-uppercut 5 times.

options: A punch that comes up from below
quiz.explain: An uppercut rises from below.

quiz.q: What turns when you throw an uppercut?
quiz.explain: Hip turn gives the uppercut power.
An uppercut aims up at the chin.

days.title: Punch a bag safely
days.goal: Learn how to hit a bag without hurting your hands.

video.title: Learn Shadow Boxing at Home in 15 Minutes

steps: Wrap your hands or wear gloves.
Hit with the front of your fist, not your fingers.
Keep your wrist straight when you punch.
Start with light punches and build up.
days.task: Practise light bag punches for 2 minutes.
days.challenge: Check your wrist stays straight after each punch.

options: To protect your knuckles and wrists
quiz.explain: Wraps protect hands from injury.

quiz.q: What part of the fist should hit?
quiz.explain: Front knuckles spread the force safely.

options: A bent wrist can get hurt
quiz.explain: A straight wrist protects the joint.

days.title: Boxing fitness: jump rope
days.goal: Learn to skip rope, the boxer's favourite warm-up.

video.title: 20-Min BOXING HIIT Workout at Home

steps: Hold the rope handles lightly.
Jump small, on the balls of your feet.
Turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms.
Skip for 1 minute, rest, repeat 3 times.
days.task: Skip for 1 minute, 3 times.
days.challenge: Skip for 2 minutes without stopping.

options: It builds footwork, timing and stamina
quiz.explain: Skipping trains feet, timing and heart.

options: Small jumps on the balls of your feet
quiz.explain: Small jumps keep you light and fast.
Wrist turns keep the rope smooth.

days.title: Boxing combos: put it together
days.goal: Learn longer combos with punches and defence.

video.title: Boxing Workout at Home: Punch, Defend, Counter in 15 Minutes

steps: Try jab-cross-hook-uppercut: 1-2-3-4.
Try jab-jab-cross: 1-1-2.
Add a slip after each combo.
Practise slowly 10 times each.
days.task: Do each combo 10 times slowly.
days.challenge: Do the combos to a steady beat.

quiz.explain: One-one-two is jab, jab, cross.

quiz.q: Why add a slip after a combo?
quiz.explain: A slip after a combo keeps you safe.

quiz.q: How should you learn a long combo?
options: Slowly, one punch at a time
quiz.explain: Slow, piece by piece builds the combo.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your 3-round workout
days.goal: Put week 2 together: build a 3-round boxing workout.

video.title: Basics of Boxing - Training for Beginners at Home

steps: Round 1: shadow boxing, 2 minutes.
Round 2: bag work or combos, 2 minutes.
Round 3: footwork and defence, 2 minutes.
Rest 1 minute between rounds.
days.task: Do your 3-round workout.
days.challenge: Do it twice this week.

quiz.q: What should a boxing workout have?
options: Shadow boxing, bag work and footwork
quiz.explain: A full workout trains punches, defence and feet.

quiz.q: How long should a round be?
quiz.explain: Two-minute rounds suit a beginner.

quiz.q: How long should you rest between rounds?
quiz.explain: A minute of rest lets you recover.

project.title: Your 3-round workout
project.brief: Build a 3-round boxing workout: shadow boxing, bag work and footwork, 2 minutes each, with 1 minute rest between rounds.

days.title: Boxing fitness: push-ups and squats
days.goal: Build strength for boxing with bodyweight moves.

video.title: How to Box 101 | Complete Boxing Tutorial for Beginners

steps: Do 10 squats and 5 push-ups.
Rest 1 minute and repeat once.
Add a 20-second plank.
Do this 2 times this week.
days.task: Do 2 rounds of squats, push-ups and plank.
days.challenge: Add 2 reps to each move next time.

quiz.q: Why do boxers need leg strength?
quiz.explain: Strong legs power punches and movement.

quiz.q: What is a good boxer strength move?
quiz.explain: Squats build the legs boxers need.

quiz.q: How often should you do strength?
quiz.explain: Twice a week is enough to help.

days.title: Defence: bob and weave
days.goal: Learn to duck under a punch safely.

video.title: Beginner to Boxer in 25 Minutes

steps: Bend your knees and dip your body down.
Move your head in a small U shape.
Keep your hands up the whole time.
Come back up to guard.
days.task: Practise 10 bobs and weaves slowly.
days.challenge: Add a bob and weave after your combo.

options: Ducking under a punch in a U shape
quiz.explain: Bob and weave ducks under punches.
Hands up keep you safe while ducking.
Bent knees let you dip low.

days.title: Speed: fast hands drill
days.goal: Learn a drill that makes your hands faster.

video.title: Learn to Box at Home: 5 Days to Master the Basics

steps: Throw jab-cross as fast as you can for 10 seconds.
Rest for 20 seconds.
Repeat 5 times.
Keep your form good even when fast.
days.task: Do 5 rounds of 10 seconds fast punches.
days.challenge: Count how many punches you throw in 10 seconds.

quiz.q: How do you get faster hands?
quiz.explain: Fast bursts train speed.
Rest stops form falling apart.

quiz.q: What matters more: speed or form?
quiz.explain: Good form makes speed safe and real.

days.title: Boxing footwork drills
days.goal: Practise footwork drills that make you move better.

video.title: Boxing for Beginners

steps: Do ladder steps: quick small steps forward and back.
Do side steps: move side to side in stance.
Do pivot turns: turn on your front foot.
Do each drill for 1 minute.
days.task: Do each footwork drill for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Combine footwork with punches for 2 minutes.

quiz.explain: A pivot turns your body without moving your feet.

options: They make your movement fast and balanced
quiz.explain: Footwork drills build speed and balance.

quiz.q: What should your feet never do?
quiz.explain: Crossed feet lose balance.

days.title: Stay safe: boxing rules
days.goal: Learn the safety rules of boxing.

video.title: Shadow Boxing for Beginners

steps: Never punch someone who is not ready.
Always wear wraps or gloves when hitting a bag.
Stop if you feel dizzy or in pain.
Respect your training partner at all times.
days.task: Write the 4 safety rules on a card.
days.challenge: Tell a friend the safety rules.

quiz.explain: Wraps and gloves protect hands.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel dizzy?
quiz.explain: Dizziness means stop and rest.

options: It is a rule with no reason
Boxing is built on trust and safety
quiz.explain: Respect keeps training safe for everyone.

days.title: Boxing combos with defence
days.goal: Put punches and defence together.

video.title: Punching and Footwork for Beginners

steps: Throw jab-cross, then slip to the side.
Throw hook-uppercut, then bob and weave.
Throw 1-2-3, then step back to guard.
Practise slowly 10 times each.
days.task: Do each punch-defence combo 10 times.
days.challenge: Do the combos to a steady beat.

quiz.q: Why add defence after a combo?
quiz.explain: Defence after attack keeps you safe.

quiz.q: What should you do after a combo?
options: Slip, weave or step back to guard
quiz.explain: Returning to guard keeps you safe.

quiz.q: How should you learn a new combo?
options: Slowly, one piece at a time
quiz.explain: Slow, piece by piece builds the combo.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your boxing circuit
days.goal: Put week 3 together: build a boxing circuit.

video.title: Learning to Box: The Basics

steps: Station 1: shadow boxing, 2 minutes.
Station 2: bag work, 2 minutes.
Station 3: skipping, 2 minutes.
Station 4: strength moves, 2 minutes.
days.task: Do your boxing circuit once.
days.challenge: Do it twice this week.

quiz.explain: A circuit links stations together.

quiz.q: How long should each station be?
quiz.explain: Two minutes per station suits a beginner.

quiz.q: What should you do between stations?
quiz.explain: A short rest keeps the circuit safe.

project.title: Your boxing circuit
project.brief: Build a boxing circuit with 4 stations: shadow boxing, bag work, skipping and strength, 2 minutes each.
checks: Did it twice in the week

days.title: Test your boxing skills
days.goal: Test how much you have learned.

video.title: BOXING BASICS (Beginner Friendly)

steps: Count how many jabs you can throw in 30 seconds with good form.
Count how many rounds you can shadow box.
Ask a friend to check your stance.
Write all three results down.
days.task: Record your 3 test results today.
days.challenge: Beat one result next week.

options: To see how much you have learned
quiz.explain: Tests show progress.

quiz.q: What matters most in a test?
quiz.explain: Good form shows true skill.
A few weeks apart shows real change.

days.title: Boxing history: learn the greats
days.goal: Learn about famous boxers and what made them great.

video.title: Low Impact Boxing Workout For Beginners

steps: Watch a short video about a famous boxer.
Write down 3 things that made them great.
Pick one thing to copy in your training.
Tell a friend about the boxer.
days.task: Write 3 things that made a great boxer great.
days.challenge: Pick one thing to copy this week.

options: It teaches lessons from the greats
quiz.explain: History shows what greatness looks like.

options: Hard work, discipline and smart defence
quiz.explain: Work, discipline and defence made them great.

quiz.q: What should you copy from a great boxer?
quiz.explain: One habit at a time is doable.

days.title: Keep training: your routine
days.goal: Make boxing a weekly habit.

video.title: Learn Shadow Boxing at Home in 15 Minutes

steps: Train 3 times a week, even if short.
Join a local boxing gym or class.
Set a new goal: learn a new combo.
Write your weekly boxing plan.
days.task: Write your weekly boxing plan.
days.challenge: Train 3 times this week.

quiz.explain: Three times a week keeps the habit alive.

options: A coach and partners help you improve
quiz.explain: A gym gives coaching and sparring partners.

quiz.q: What is a good next goal?
quiz.explain: A new combo keeps you growing.

days.title: Boxing with a partner: pad work
days.goal: Learn simple pad work with a partner.

video.title: 20-Min BOXING HIIT Workout at Home

steps: One person holds pads, the other punches.
Start with the jab only.
The holder calls out 'one' for a jab.
Swap roles after 1 minute.
Keep punches light and controlled.
Rest 30 seconds between rounds.
days.task: Do 3 rounds of pad work with a friend.
days.challenge: Add the cross: 'one-two'.

options: Punching pads that a partner holds
quiz.explain: Pad work lets you practise punches safely with a partner.

quiz.q: Why start with the jab only?
options: So you learn one punch well first
quiz.explain: One punch at a time builds clean skill.
Swapping often keeps both partners learning.

days.title: Boxing fitness: squats and burpees
days.goal: Learn two moves that build boxing fitness.

video.title: Boxing Workout at Home: Punch, Defend, Counter in 15 Minutes

steps: Do 10 squats.
Do 5 burpees: squat, jump back to a plank, jump forward, stand up.
Rest for 30 seconds.
Repeat 3 times.
Breathe out on the hard part.
Stop if you feel dizzy.
days.task: Do the squat and burpee circuit today.
days.challenge: Do 4 rounds next week.

options: A squat, a jump back, a push-up and a jump
quiz.explain: A burpee works the whole body in one move.
Short rests keep the workout safe and strong.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel dizzy?
quiz.explain: Stopping when dizzy keeps you safe.

days.title: Watch a boxing match and learn
days.goal: Learn by watching real boxers.

video.title: Basics of Boxing - Training for Beginners at Home

steps: Watch 10 minutes of a boxing match.
Watch the boxer's feet, not just the punches.
Notice how they move in and out.
Write down one move they use well.
Try that move in shadow boxing.
Watch another match next week.
days.task: Watch 10 minutes of a boxing match.
days.challenge: Copy one move you saw into your shadow boxing.

quiz.q: What should you watch besides punches?
quiz.explain: Footwork is half of boxing.

options: So you remember it and can practise it
quiz.explain: Writing it down locks the lesson in.

quiz.q: What should you do after watching?
options: Try the move in shadow boxing
quiz.explain: Trying the move turns watching into learning.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final show.

video.title: How to Box 101 | Complete Boxing Tutorial for Beginners

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 skills you can now do.
Practise your capstone routine once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 boxing skills you learned.
days.challenge: Do your capstone routine from memory.

options: A final show that proves what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can shadow box a full routine safely
quiz.explain: A full routine done well shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest.

video.title: Beginner to Boxer in 25 Minutes

steps: Shadow box your capstone routine one more time.
Check your stance, your guard and your footwork.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Shadow box your capstone routine and time it.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

options: Practice makes the real show calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
quiz.explain: Checking stance and guard makes it smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you perform your best.

days.title: Capstone day: your boxing routine
days.goal: Show what you learned: perform your boxing routine.

video.title: Learn to Box at Home: 5 Days to Master the Basics

steps: Warm up with skipping for 2 minutes.
Shadow box your routine: stance, jabs, crosses, hooks, defence.
Cool down with slow walking and stretching.
Write a short report on how it went.
days.task: Perform your boxing routine and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What is the first step of your routine?
quiz.explain: A warm-up gets the body ready.

quiz.q: What matters most in the routine?
options: Going as fast as you can
Good form, guard up and smooth footwork
quiz.explain: Form, guard and footwork show real skill.

options: What you did and how it felt
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Your boxing routine
capstone.brief: Perform your boxing routine: warm-up with skipping, shadow boxing with stance, jabs, crosses, hooks and defence, cool-down, and a short written report.
checks: Threw jab, cross and hook well
deliverables: A short video or notes from the routine
